subject: Request: Full purge of prompts/outputs/logs — confirmation & timeline
messages:
From: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acmehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 02 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: purge of prompts/outputs/logs (Acme account)

Hi Monica,

We need to initiate a full purge request under our DPA for the Acme Health production workspace (org id: ACME-2190). Specifically:
- All user prompts and model outputs associated with the Acme Health workspace since onboarding (2024-05-01).
- Inference logs and telemetry tied to that workspace (request traces, token logs).
- Any KV cache or ephemeral prompt caches stored in your hosted runtime for our sessions.

Please confirm:
1) What exactly you will remove vs what remains for retention/backups (and why).
2) Timeline and SLA for completion.
3) Proof/certificate of deletion and an audit record we can attach to our internal compliance artifact.
4) Any steps we need to take on our side to avoid re-ingestion or to make sure the deletion is scoped correctly.

I’ve looped in our legal mailbox. We may need a short DPA amendment to document the expedited purge and confirmation email content — attaching a redline in my next email if helpful.

Thanks,
Sarah Jensen
Director, Data Privacy & Compliance
Acme Health

Subject: Re: Request: purge of prompts/outputs/logs (Acme account)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear scope. We can do this; outlining the practical workflow below so expectations align. I’m attaching our deletion SOP for reference.

Summary of steps (hosted Redwood API):
1) Scope verification: we will lock the Acme workspace and capture the list of active model endpoints, buckets, and job IDs for the purge window. We’ll ask you to confirm if any subsets should be excluded.
2) Active data purge: remove prompt text and generated outputs from our primary document store (S3) and from indexing services. This typically covers customer-supplied inputs and model responses.
3) Runtime caches: evict KV caches and ephemeral session caches from the serving runtime (this invalidates in-memory caches and any persisted checkpoint files).
4) Telemetry/logs: delete request-level logs from the fast-logging pipeline and mark associated BigQuery/analytics exports for deletion. Note: aggregated metrics (rollups) remain but will not contain prompt/text payloads.
5) Backups & snapshots: we will identify backups and snapshots; depending on backup immutability windows, full destruction may be impossible for backups older than 30 days, but we will ensure they are made inaccessible and document the reason.
6) Audit record: we will generate a deletion certificate (internal ticket + hash list of removed objects) and provide an audit bundle (ticket link + confirmation email).

Estimated timeline: 3–5 business days after you confirm final scope. If you request expedited handling we can prioritize and aim for 48–72 hours but require sign-off from the legal/compliance teams.

Please confirm the following so we can begin:
- Final scope (all endpoints? specific datasets?)
- Preferred SLA (standard 3–5 days or expedited 48–72h)

We’ll also need to know whether any logs are retained by your SIEM/exporters separately (so we don’t miss external copies).

Attaching: data-deletion-SOP.pdf (internal playbook + checklist).

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Lead — Key Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: purge of prompts/outputs/logs (Acme account)

Thanks Monica — adding a technical breakdown so Acme knows exactly what we’ll touch.

Technical purge plan (hosted):
- Object store (S3): delete object keys tagged with org=ACME-2190 and time range <= 2025-11-02. We will run a dry-run first and provide a list of keys to Sarah for confirmation.
- Serving runtime caches: for each GPU node that served ACME traffic we will run a cache-evict sweep and rotate key namespaces. This ensures in-memory KV and local disk caches are cleared.
- Logging pipeline: remove entries in the fast-logging index and submit deletion jobs for BigQuery tables (we will use partition drop for date ranges).
- Indexes & search: remove any embeddings or indexes derived from prompts/outputs. These are independent stored artifacts and will be enumerated in the dry-run.
- Backups: snapshots older than retention will be marked for destruction; for immutable snapshots we will mark them inaccessible and include the rationale in the certificate.

Important notes:
- Immutable snapshots: some of our controlled backups have write-once windows managed by third-party cloud providers. In practice those cannot be retroactively zeroed; we document and certify in the deletion report that they remain under vendor-controlled retention but are logically inaccessible to Redwood runtime.
- Auditability: each deletion job will generate a manifest file with object IDs and SHA256 digests; we will store the manifest in a sealed audit bucket and share a signed deletion certificate (PDF).

Request ID (for this operation): THR-17C9
Dry-run report due: 2025-11-03T18:00:00-08:00
Estimated completion (expedited confirmed): 2025-11-05T17:00:00-08:00

Hi Sarah — quick update and confirmation: the purge jobs for org ACME-2190 completed today. Summary below plus links to the audit bundle.

What we removed:
- Prompt text and model outputs stored in primary object storage for the requested window (2024-05-01 through 2025-11-02).
- Runtime KV caches and ephemeral session caches across all serving hosts that handled ACME traffic.
- Request-level logs and telemetry entries in the fast-logging pipeline for the date range; corresponding BigQuery partitions have been dropped.
- Embeddings and search indexes derived from prompts/outputs for the workspace.

What remains (and why):
- Immutable vendor-managed snapshots older than 30 days: these are controlled by the cloud provider and marked inaccessible to Redwood. We cannot retroactively edit vendor immutable blobs; we have documented them in the certificate and included the snapshot IDs.
- Aggregated telemetry: anonymized rollups and product-level metrics remain (no prompt or output text in rollups).

Audit bundle provided: 
- Deletion certificate (signed): deletion_certificate-THR17C9.pdf
- Manifest (SHA256 list) and dry-run report: attached to ticket THR-17C9 (link below)
- Ticket link with logs of the jobs and timestamps: https://redwood.app/tickets/THR-17C9

Sample confirmation email we used (you may attach this to your compliance artifacts):
"\nSubject: Redwood deletion confirmation — ACME-2190 (THR-17C9)\nBody: Redwood Inference confirms that, as of 2025-11-05T16:42:00-08:00, the following data associated with Acme Health org ACME-2190 has been removed from production-accessible stores: prompt text, model outputs, runtime caches, request-level telemetry (specified partitions), and derived indexes. Immutable vendor-managed snapshots older than 30 days remain vendor-controlled and have been documented in the attached certificate. Deletion manifest and signed certificate attached. Request ID: THR-17C9.\n"

If you need a notarized signature or additional e-signature on the certificate we can route to Legal.

Thanks for the quick coordination. Closing this from the account team side; please reply if anything else is needed.

—Monica
